Omit login only for an installation with exactly one administrator; otherwise supply an existing administrator from getAdminAccount(). Password and login are sensitive and sent in the POST body. Upstream accepts any nonempty password without its own strength rule.

The source describes passing the password through a caller-private file without process-list, process-environment or WordPress Toolkit log exposure. This is documented behavior, not observed live evidence.

Creates a cPanel API token and a Nova magic link; it neither installs WordPress nor queues an installation. A later importWebsite callback starts the import. Requires nova-wordpress, mysql, redirects, apitokens and disk headroom; the source says it does not enforce the WordPress website-count limit. The source attributes token revocation on Nova failure; this is not live evidence. Collision queues nothing.

promptToken is opaque caller-supplied base64: upstream supports standard/URL-safe variants with optional padding, at most 8192 sent characters and 5000 decoded bytes. The client never decodes or re-encodes. Omission or a blank prompt may consume a session prompt; a supplied nonblank prompt leaves that fallback intact.

Upstream returnUrl must be HTTPS on the same cPanel host, with no userinfo and at most 2048 characters. Invalid values are ignored for a default, not rejected locally. The prompt, return URL and returned magic link are private; never log or fetch the magic link.
